title.en: Geography: Climate and Natural Vegetation of India

text.en: Raju felt a hot summer wind. "What decides India's climate?" he asked.

India has a tropical monsoon climate with four seasons: winter, summer, the south-west monsoon and the retreating north-east monsoon. Factors affecting it are latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, the monsoon winds and relief.
The south-west monsoon brings most of India's rain between June and September. Tamil Nadu gets much of its rain from the north-east monsoon in October to December. Cyclones form in the Bay of Bengal.
Natural vegetation includes tropical evergreen, deciduous, thorn, mountain and mangrove forests. Mangroves grow in deltas such as the Sundarbans, while the Western Ghats have evergreen forests. Forests are conserved to protect wildlife.

problem.en: Why does Tamil Nadu get rain in winter?

text.en: North-east monsoon winds blow from the sea.
They bring rain in Oct to Dec.
So the state is wet then.
